source: The `oneharness` history this host records for every `just review-plan` turn: `$XDG_STATE_HOME/oneharness/history/<project>/you-are-reviewing-one-task-of-*.jsonl`, which `oneharness.plan-review.toml`'s `history = true` writes. Only a pass is recorded onto a plan's task, so a refusal survives nowhere else.
selection: Every recorded plan-review turn of this repository's own checkouts whose answer parsed as a verdict and whose `passes` was false, at the cutoff below. 721 verdicts were recorded in all; 367 of them refused.
cutoff: 2026-09-05T00:00:00Z, the last review turn recorded before this change was dispatched.
base: 8b695645f67e650fc6495b69a30e554ffef6fb3f, the commit the widening below started from. `already-caught` and `newly-caught` were decided by running `orchestrator/criteria_guard.py` from that commit and from the finished tree over each refusal's own reviewed task.

classifications.already-caught: `orchestrator/criteria_guard.py` refused this task's criteria on the commit this dispatch started from, so the judged turn that produced the refusal need not have been spent.
classifications.newly-caught: The detectors this change widens refuse it on the finished tree and did not refuse it on that base.
classifications.left-to-the-judge: No detector refuses it, and the shape's `false_refusal_risk` below says what a detector for it would refuse that ought to pass.

goal-not-proved.what: The criteria could all be satisfied while the goal the task states is missed.
goal-not-proved.false_refusal_risk: Deciding it needs a model of the goal and of what each criterion admits. The nearest deterministic form refuses a criterion that permits an alternative outcome — which is the shape of every sound conditional criterion this repository writes, `or is unchanged, in which case the finished tree records what refused it` among them.

procedure.what: The criterion prescribes a development step in place of the property that step produces.
procedure.false_refusal_risk: Past the red-before-green idiom the shape is ordinary prose. The general form keys on `is run` / `has been run`, which the recorded corpus carries in 22 tasks that passed review as well as 23 that were refused: it would refuse `the container the script runs is given the invoking user's uid`, which states a property.

outside-dispatch.what: The criterion rests on state the worker's own dispatch does not reach.
outside-dispatch.false_refusal_risk: What the remainder rests on is a live external service, a nondeterministic tier, or another node's landing, and none of those is lexically distinct from a property of the finished tree. Both nearest deterministic forms refuse sound criteria: `the judged lint over this diff is green` is a criterion this repository's own nodes state and pass review with, and `is merged` would refuse `Nothing is merged, pushed, or opened` — a criterion asserting the dispatch merges nothing, which the corpus carries on a refused and a passed version of one task alike.

perishable.what: The criterion pins to a fact that can move on its own between the task being written and its node being dispatched.
perishable.false_refusal_risk: `VERSION_LITERAL` already refuses the spelled-out number. What is left is prose — `the newest release it could take`, `what GitHub requires today` — and refusing `the newest release` would refuse the exact criterion `tests/test_criteria_guard.py::test_a_criterion_naming_the_property_instead_is_accepted` holds up as the correct replacement for a version literal.

mutually-unsatisfiable.what: Two criteria of the same task cannot both hold for some outcome the task itself allows.
mutually-unsatisfiable.false_refusal_risk: Deciding it means reasoning over criterion pairs and over the outcomes the task admits. Every lexical proxy reduces to refusing criteria that name one subject twice, which is what a task stating two properties of one artifact does.

unfalsifiable.what: No fixture, input, or repository state would make the criterion fail, so it can never be what stops bad work.
unfalsifiable.false_refusal_risk: It is decided by looking for a falsifying state, which is a reading of the criterion's subject. Any proxy — a criterion naming no fixture, no file, no command — refuses the properly abstract property criteria that are most of a sound plan.

repository-wide-gate.what: The criterion makes a repository-wide gate an acceptance condition, where the bar asks for the checks that exercise this change.
repository-wide-gate.false_refusal_risk: Where it names `just check` the procedure detector already refuses it. The rest names a project's own target — `shell:lint` — and refusing target-shaped tokens would refuse a criterion naming the target the change itself adds.

spelling.what: The criterion demands a particular string rather than a particular property.
spelling.false_refusal_risk: `PHRASE` refuses the `verbatim` / `the exact wording` idiom. What is left states the same demand without those words, and refusing a criterion for quoting a vocabulary would refuse every criterion that names the value a field must carry.

demand-not-stated.what: The criteria omit a verification demand the node will be held to.
demand-not-stated.false_refusal_risk: `DEMANDS` refuses this wherever the resolved bar or the task's own prose makes the demand in words this module matches. What is left is a demand nothing in the task states at all, and an absent sentence has nothing to match on.

human-action-ambiguous.what: A `kind: human` node names a genuinely external action a person could read two ways.
human-action-ambiguous.false_refusal_risk: Whether prose is unambiguous to the person who will perform it is not a property any pattern decides.
